title: 1950 AHSME Problem 47
statement: A rectangle inscribed in a triangle has its base coinciding with the base \(b\) of the triangle. If the altitude of the triangle is \(h,\) and the altitude \(x\) of the rectangle is half the base of the rectangle, then:

solutions.text:
By similarity, the width of the triangle at height \(x\) above its base is \(b(1-\tfrac{x}{h}).\) This is the base of the inscribed rectangle. Since the rectangle’s altitude is half its base, its base is \(2x.\) Hence \[ 2x=b\left(1-\frac{x}{h}\right). \] Multiplying by \(h\) and solving gives \(x(2h+b)=bh,\) so \(x=\dfrac{bh}{2h+b}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: The segment across the triangle at height \(x\) has length \(b(1-\frac{x}{h})\)
